result.topic_en: For an imaginary root r(cos φ + i sin φ) of the trinomial equation x^{α+β} − p x^α + q = 0, the page expresses the powers of the modulus r in terms of sines of multiples of the angle φ, and gives the equation that determines φ.
result.transcription:
Math 20 \quad (5) [-45b/6-]

Es sei $r(\cos\varphi + i\sin\varphi)$ eine imaginäre Wurzel der
Gleichung mit drei Gliedern
$x^{\alpha+\beta} - px^{\alpha} + q = 0$ \quad Wurzel in üblicher Bedeutg

Es ist dann
$r^{\alpha+\beta} = \frac{q\sin\alpha\varphi}{\sin\beta\varphi}$ \quad $\frac{\sin\alpha\varphi}{r^{\alpha+\beta}} = \frac{\sin\beta\varphi}{q} = \frac{\sin(\alpha+\beta)\varphi}{pr^{\alpha}}$
$r^{\alpha} = \frac{q\sin(\alpha+\beta)\varphi}{p\sin\beta\varphi}$
$r^{\beta} = \frac{p\sin\alpha\varphi}{\sin(\alpha+\beta)\varphi}$
wo $\varphi$ aus der Gleichung

$q^{\beta}\cdot\sin(\alpha+\beta)\varphi^{\alpha+\beta} = p^{\alpha+\beta}\cdot\sin\alpha\varphi^{\alpha}\cdot\sin\beta\varphi^{\beta}$
bestimmt wird.

methods.what: Modulus of a complex root of the trinomial x^{α+β} − p x^α + q = 0 expressed through sines of multiples of its argument (from the imaginary part of the equation, via de Moivre)
Proportionality relation among the sine terms derived from the trinomial
Formula for r^α in terms of φ
Formula for r^β in terms of φ
Transcendental equation determining the argument φ of the root (elimination of r)

items.english: It then holds that r^{α+β} = q sin αφ / sin βφ (together with the following formulas for r^α and r^β).

items.quote:
wo $\varphi$ aus der Gleichung

$q^{\beta}\cdot\sin(\alpha+\beta)\varphi^{\alpha+\beta} = p^{\alpha+\beta}\cdot\sin\alpha\varphi^{\alpha}\cdot\sin\beta\varphi^{\beta}$
bestimmt wird.
